title: SYNDACTYLY, TYPE III
alt_titles: SYNDACTYLY OF FINGERS IV AND V

intro.text: This entry describes type III syndactyly (SDTY3), an autosomal dominant hand malformation with syndactyly of the ring and little fingers. Linkage to chromosome 6q22-q24, the region containing the oculodentodigital dysplasia locus, has been suggested, but the papers cited here do not identify a causal gene for isolated type III syndactyly.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly (SDTY3) is an autosomal dominant hand malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: Five new cases of isolated syndactyly of the small and ring finger are described. Autosomal dominant inheritance is obvious.
checks.explanation: The paper describes ring-small finger syndactyly with obvious autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features, further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.
checks.explanation: The abstract suggests the isolated type III syndactyly locus lies in the same region as ODD, which the title places at 6q22-q24.

paragraphs.text: Type III syndactyly is syndactyly of the ring and little fingers (Johnston and Kirby, 1955). It is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait with variable expression (McKiernan and McCann, 1993). Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is often present (De Smet et al., 1994). Type III syndactyly also occurs as part of oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODD), and how the isolated form relates to ODD has been discussed (Brueton et al., 1990; Schrander-Stumpel et al., 1993; Gladwin et al., 1997).

checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied. It confirms the paper is about syndactyly of the ring and little finger, but it never uses the 'type III' classification or defines that type.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.explanation: The paper confirms autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.explanation: The paper reports variable phenotypic expression.

checks.evidence_quote: Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is a frequent association.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly also occurs as part of oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODD).
checks.evidence_quote: The present family provides evidence of the variable expression in oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The title calls type III syndactyly and ODD a clinical spectrum. The authors also read this syndactyly family as showing variable expression of ODD. Together these mean the paper treats type III syndactyly as part of ODD.

paragraphs.text: Opjordsmoen and Nyberg-Hansen (1980) reported a family from northern Norway with a hereditary neurologic disorder made up of spastic paraplegia, neurogenic bladder disturbances, and syndactyly. Nine of 22 family members across 3 generations had these features. The bladder disturbance was an incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis (uninhibited neurogenic bladder). It was the main complaint and appeared early in the disease. The authors thought the family probably had an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia.

checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; 'syndactylia' is the same as syndactyly.

None of the other characteristic findings of oculodentodigital dysplasia were present. The authors discussed the relationship between type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) reported a newborn boy with complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3 to 5 on the left hand and fingers 4 and 5 on the right hand. His mother and maternal grandmother had been born with the same hand malformation. The mother had a thin nose and small teeth, and her eyes were normal. The grandmother had had very small teeth with enamel hypoplasia, and her eyes were normal. The authors considered that the family showed the variable expression of oculodentodigital dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: McKiernan and McCann (1993) reported a pedigree with 14 cases of familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger. Three were treated surgically in their unit, and a fourth had earlier been treated elsewhere by the senior author. Clinical study showed variable phenotypic expression.

paragraphs.text: Gladwin et al. (1997) used a genome-wide search to map oculodentodigital syndrome to chromosome 6q22-q24 (maximum pairwise lod score = 9.37 at theta = 0.001). Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly also maps to this region.
